title: Introduce priority token lanes and invocation trellis dashboard for fine-grained cost/latency attribution
author: Ananya Rao
description: Motivation: We currently attribute token cost and latency at the invocation level, but important operational signal is lost when tokens with different runtime priorities are aggregated (e.g., user-interactive vs background prefetch vs system prompts). This PR introduces a lightweight runtime tag — priority token lanes — plus an invocation trellis visualization to expose per-lane token counts, cost, and latency timelines. Summary of changes: (1) Runtime: add token_priority enum and propagate as a per-token metadata bit in the invocation envelope; metrics emitter tags token counters and histogram labels with priority_lane; tracing: add lane-aware spans and a compact lane ID to trace attributes; (2) Metrics: instrument lane-scoped counters, p99/p50 token-latency histograms per lane, lane-tagged CPU/GPU kernel time estimates; (3) Dashboards: new "Invocation Trellis" dashboard that lays out lane timelines across an invocation, plus a cost breakdown panel that slices spend by lane and model stage; (4) Alerts: add SLO-oriented alert rule templates that optionally ignore low-priority lanes (configurable) and a lane-based suppression gate for noisy background workloads; (5) Telemetry rollout and compatibility: metrics use new tag priority_lane with a fallback value "unspecified" to preserve compatibility; all changes are guarded behind a feature flag telemetry.priority_lanes with gradual rollout. Implementation notes and decisions: - We chose an enumerated lane set (interactive, background_prefetch, system, analytic) to limit cardinality and make aggregation simple. - Token-level tagging is emitted only for the first token of each contiguous lane segment by default (sampling path) to avoid high cardinality in high-throughput paths; full token tagging can be enabled for debug traces. - Tracing adds a short lane_id to spans (1 byte) to keep overhead low; OpenTelemetry attributes are used so downstream collectors can use the tag. Rollout plan: start feature-flagged in staging for 48h (telemetry.priority_lanes=partial), run synthetic generation at 100inv/s and evaluate cost deltas; open to 10% of production traffic after gating on no perf regressions and <0.5% increase in metric cardinality. Migration notes for users: dashboards are opt-in for accounts; customers who use tenant-level billing reports will see lane slices only after the platform enables the flag for their tenant. Checklist: - [x] Runtime token tag + propagation - [x] Lane-aware metrics and histograms - [x] Invocation Trellis Grafana dashboard JSON - [x] Alert templates and runbook additions - [x] Unit + integration tests for tag propagation - [x] Perf microbenchmarks and budget evaluation - [x] Feature flag gating and staged rollout Testing performed: unit tests for envelope propagation, integration tests against a local collectd and jaeger stack, performance microbench comparing main runtime with and without lane tagging (median latency diff +0.3%). Known limitations: high-cardinality workloads that enable full per-token tagging may increase cardinality — we provide a limiter configuration. Future work: auto-classify lanes based on request metadata and a per-tenant sampling policy for lane tagging.

Lena Schmidt: Please add a runbook entry describing expected cost delta (response: added runbook note and release notes)

release_notes:
- Added priority token lanes (interactive, background_prefetch, system, analytic) for finer cost and latency attribution.
- New 'Invocation Trellis' dashboard for per-invocation lane timelines and lane-sliced cost panels.
- Lane-aware SLO templates and alert suppression gates.
- Feature gated (telemetry.priority_lanes) with staged rollout to control cardinality.
